svg.title: Not My Will
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (Luke 22:41-42): at night on the Mount of Olives Jesus kneels alone, the sleeping disciples a stone's throw off. Caption: "The Mount of Olives. He withdraws a stone’s throw, kneels and prays." Jesus says: "Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done." Panel 2 (Matthew 26:40-41): Jesus stands over Peter, who has been sleeping. Jesus says: "Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation." Panel 3 (Matthew 26:42): Jesus kneels again alone, praying. Caption: "A second time, the words He taught them (Matthew 6:10):". Jesus says: "My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done." Panel 4 (Luke 23:33, 46): three crosses on a rise under a darkened sky. Caption: "The cup is not taken away. His last words are a prayer." Jesus says: "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!" Panel 5 (Hebrews 5:7; Luke 24:5-6): the tomb open at dawn, its stone rolled back. Caption: "“He was heard because of his reverence.” (Hebrews 5:7)". The two men at the tomb says: "He is not here, but has risen." Note: "Heard: read here, with the ESV Study Bible, as the resurrection." The point: The Father did not take the cup from His Son Jesus. He heard Him, and He raised Him from the dead. So you can pray “your will be done” and leave the outcome with Him (Hebrews 5:7).
svg.text: Gethsemane, the cross and the empty tomb in one minute
